transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-18 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (Mercury CTO), Leo Zhang (Mercury DevOps), Priya Menon (Mercury PM)
Recording id: ff-20250318-mercury-console-01

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Redwood walked through Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdowns.
- Mercury asked about cost attribution, tagging, RBAC, and private deployment options for PHI.
- Agreed to run per-route cost analysis and share security docs; pilot kickoff tentatively next week.

Topics covered:
- Per-route dashboards and filters (app, user, route)
- Token-level cost breakdown and billing export
- Tagging and billing attribution for teams
- Alerts/abnormal usage detection and cost anomalies
- Dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs and SLAs
- Data residency and SOC2/KMS concerns for PHI

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we can probably start, um, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Carlos my colleague will do the deep dive into the Console dashboards.
[00:00:12] Anita: Hi Maya, thanks. We only have 50 mins so appreciate the tight agenda.
[00:00:18] Carlos: Great, I'll share my screen. Give me a sec, window list... okay visible? I'm in the Redwood Console org "Mercury-demo" that we pre-populated.
[00:00:28] Priya: Yep it's visible, I see the left nav.
[00:00:32] Carlos: Cool. First screen is the usage overview — high-level tokens in, tokens out, 7-day trend. You'll notice we show per-model and per-route breakdowns side-by-side.
[00:00:45] Leo: Quick question, when you say route is that the API route path we send in the header or is it the model + prompt type?
[00:00:52] Carlos: Good Q. We map routes based on your application-level route name (you set it in the SDK header) and also annotate with model id and config. So you get route-level aggregation and model-level aggregation. There can be overlapping filters.
[00:01:05] Maya: And that mapping is what lets you get cost-by-feature — e.g., chat-widget vs batch-embeddings.
[00:01:09] Anita: We need that because billing is split across clinical apps and research teams.
[00:01:14] Carlos: Exactly. Now I'll click into "Per-route dashboard". This shows each route as a card with throughput, median latency, p95, token count and estimated cost.
[00:01:27] [00:01:27] (transcription artifact: "per route" read as "per root")
[00:01:30] Priya: The estimated cost column — how is that calculated? Are we seeing list prices or post-discount?
[00:01:37] Carlos: By default the Console shows list unit cost multiplied by token counts. If you have a committed contract (Dedicated or volume discounts), we can apply your pricing profile server-side so the dashboard reflects discounted unit costs. We store pricing profiles at account level.
[00:01:52] Leo: Can we import our internal chargeback rates? We have slightly different rates per team.
[00:01:57] Carlos: Yes, you can either enter chargeback multipliers in the Console or export CSV and push to your internal billing system. We also support tagging per-request (X-Org-Tag) that gets stored and shows up as a filter.
[00:02:08] Anita: Is tagging enforced? If a dev forgets the header will it default?
[00:02:12] Carlos: You can set a default route and default tags at the SDK level; Redwood will label unlabeled traffic as "unattributed" and you can set alerts if unattributed > X%.
[00:02:20] Maya: I'll point out the cost breakdown view — token-level lines show input vs output tokens, spent compute, and a small column estimating GPU-time equivalent. That last piece helps you understand when longer context windows are the cost driver.
[00:02:31] [00:02:31] (speaker overlap; possible mislabeling)
[00:02:35] Priya: On that note, we have a lot of long chats from clinical intake forms. Does Redwood show per-request sequence length distribution?
[00:02:43] Carlos: Yes, histogram on the right shows sequence length and you can click into the tail to list example requests. We also have automatic suggestions — e.g., consider prefix caching on this route, or a smaller model for non-clinical fields.
[00:02:58] Leo: Does prefix caching work with stateful chat or only stateless requests?
[00:03:03] Carlos: Works with conversation if you pin the KV key for the conversation; but for PHI you might want to avoid caching sensitive items. The Console flags cacheable candidates, but you control it.
[00:03:12] Anita: PHI is a primary concern — we need KMS + audit logs and an option to run the Console behind our VPC.
[00:03:19] Maya: Yep, that's one of the reasons we talked about Private deployment earlier. For audit logs we provide streaming to your SIEM, and the private control plane option gives you the Console inside your VPC. We'll share SOC2 docs.
[00:03:30] Carlos: Back to dashboards — here's the "Cost by Team" heatmap. It uses tags and user mappings. You can also group by project, route, or model family.
[00:03:41] Priya: Can we get this per day and export to our chargeback tool?
[00:03:44] Carlos: Exports are CSV/Parquet; we have a connector template for Snowflake and BigQuery.
[00:03:50] Leo: About alerts — can we set cost anomaly detection on a per-route basis? e.g., alert if cost/day > baseline + 3 sigma?
[00:03:58] Carlos: Yes, there's an alerts UI. You can choose baseline window (14/30/90 days) and granularity (route, model, org). Alerts can post to Slack, webhook, or ticket.
[00:04:07] Maya: I'll jump in with an example: last month a customer saw a hidden cost spike due to a prompt template change that increased output length; the Console's anomaly detection caught it and the SE rolled back the prompt.
[00:04:18] Anita: Nice. We also need down-sampled traces for debugging. Does the Console hold per-token trace or just aggregates?
[00:04:25] Carlos: We retain token-level traces for X days by default (retention policy varies by plan). For Private you can set retention; there's also a PII scrubbing option where tokens are hashed before storage.
[00:04:36] [00:04:36] (transcription: "hashing" heard as "hushing")
[00:04:40] Priya: For the dedicated vs hosted question — what's typical cost delta if we go Dedicated?
[00:04:46] Maya: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and usually lower unit cost at commit levels. Short answer: depends on committed GPU hours and utilization. Carlos can run a model-based estimate during the pilot.
[00:04:57] Carlos: Right — using your sample traffic we can simulate token volumes and model mixes. The Console will then show a projected monthly spend under hosted vs dedicated pricing.
[00:05:07] Leo: Can the Console simulate mixed routing — e.g., route A to dedicated, route B to hosted fallback on burst?
[00:05:14] Carlos: Yes, routing policies are pluggable and we surface estimated unit cost for each policy; the simulation engine will show cost & latency tradeoffs.
[00:05:21] Priya: Walk me through a per-route drill-down please.
[00:05:24] Carlos: Clicking route "clinical-intake" — top chart is tokens per minute, below is p50/p95 latency. On the right we have cost waterfall: base model cost, prefix cache savings, batching savings, and then estimated infra surcharge.
[00:05:40] [00:05:40] (minor stutter)
[00:05:44] Anita: That surcharge line — is that our dedicated infra overhead or network egress?
[00:05:49] Carlos: It can be configured. By default it's a small infra overhead that reflects additional bookkeeping; you can also add network egress or partner charges.
[00:05:56] Priya: Does Redwood do token-level unit visibility for embeddings and search? We have a heavy embeddings workload.
[00:06:03] Carlos: Yes, embeddings appear as their own model family and we show vector indexing costs separately (index build vs query). You can see cost per thousand vectors and per-query.
[00:06:12] Leo: For billing exports, can we map to our GL codes?
[00:06:16] Carlos: You can attach GL codes as tags and export them in CSV with a mapping column.
[00:06:21] Maya: Quick call-out: we also support per-token cost breakouts in the API response via metadata headers if you want to ingest meter-level data directly.
[00:06:31] Priya: Hmm that might be helpful.
[00:06:33] Anita: What about rate limiting and quotas at a route level?
[00:06:37] Carlos: We have rate limit policies per route or per API key. They can be soft throttles with a warning or hard rejects. Quotas can also be monthly token caps per team.
[00:06:45] Leo: For integrations — does Console support our SSO (Okta) and SCIM provisioning?
[00:06:50] Maya: Yes SAML/SSO via Okta supported, and we have SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC roles include Viewer, Analyst, Admin, SE/Support.
[00:06:59] Anita: Audit trail must show who changed a rate limit or a routing policy.
[00:07:04] Carlos: Audit logs show user, action, before/after, and IP; logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[00:07:10] [00:07:10] (transcription: "SIEM" mis-heard as "seam")
[00:07:14] Priya: Can we see a sample of the exported CSV?
[00:07:17] Carlos: Sure — I exported a small slice. (uploads link) Link: https://redwood-demo-links/slices/mercury-per-route-sample.csv
[00:07:25] Maya: We'll include that in the follow-up email as well.
[00:07:29] Priya: Great. About the UI, can product managers configure default dashboards per team?
[00:07:34] Carlos: Yep, dashboards are shareable and you can pin a default dashboard to an org or team. We also have saved filters and scheduled reports by email.
[00:07:42] Anita: On security again, we need to confirm encryption at rest with our KMS.
[00:07:47] Maya: For Private we integrate with customer KMS; for Hosted we use provider-managed KMS but can do envelope encryption. We'll send the KMS integration docs.
[00:07:55] Leo: Is there an option to redact PII before it hits logs?
[00:07:58] Carlos: Yes there is an optional scrubbing pipeline; you can define rules or use our built-in PII detector to hash identified PII before storage.
[00:08:06] Priya: Ok last section — Optimize tie-in. Does Redwood Optimize give automated batching/quantization suggestions and will those appear in the Console?
[00:08:15] Carlos: Optimize runs offline evals on your prompt set and, when it finds safe savings (e.g., quantized fp16 for non-critical routes), it surfaces recommendations in the Console with estimated cost savings and risk level.
[00:08:28] Maya: For example, in the demo account Optimize flagged the "search-snippet" route — suggested switching to a smaller model for short queries and enabling caching for frequent prompts. Estimated savings ~23%.
[00:08:40] Anita: How do we validate quality after Optimize suggests changes?
[00:08:44] Carlos: Optimize can run a holdout evaluation set and provide quality metrics (BLEU-like or custom success criteria). You can tie these to rollouts so canary only runs if quality delta within threshold.
[00:08:56] Priya: That solves a lot. Are there guardrails so we don't accidentally roll out to production?
[00:09:02] Carlos: Rollouts are policy-driven: canary percent, monitor windows, automatic rollback on metrics breach.
[00:09:07] Maya: Quick recap, since we're near the end: Mercury wants cost-by-feature, tagging and chargeback, RBAC/audit for compliance, KMS/Audit logs for PHI, and a pilot to run per-route cost analysis.
[00:09:20] Anita: Yes, and we'll provide sample traffic and success criteria.
[00:09:24] Leo: I'll upload the traffic today to the S3 link you shared.
[00:09:28] Maya: Thanks. Next steps we'll email the sample CSV, pricing, SOC2 whitepaper, and schedule the kickoff. Carlos will run the cost analysis and share the simulation in the Console demo org.
[00:09:38] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:09:40] Maya: Appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the artifact links.
[00:09:44] (meeting ends)
